questions.q: What are the three non-negotiable requirements for the capstone research library?
options: Pretty, popular, and portable
Fast, reproducible, and testable
Cheap, cloud-native, and asynchronous
Object-oriented, documented, and open source
questions.explain: The capstone has to be fast (vectorized, with one Numba hot path), reproducible (config-driven, seeded, logged), and testable (pytest with assert_allclose).

questions.q: According to the lesson, when should a calculation be hand-optimized with Numba?
options: Everywhere, as a default for all numerical code
Only after profiling identifies it as the actual hot path, and no vectorized alternative covers it
Only inside unit tests
Never — Numba should not appear in the capstone at all
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: Numba is reserved for the one rolling calculation that profiling shows is the hot path, not applied broadly.

questions.q: In the three-layer architecture, which statement correctly describes how the layers interact?
options: Data flows one direction only: data layer to computation layer to reporting layer
The reporting layer re-reads raw prices directly from Parquet
The computation layer loads its own data independently of the data layer
All three layers live in a single module with no separation
questions.explain: The architecture keeps responsibilities separated with one-way data flow, which is what makes each layer independently testable.

questions.q: Which of these is explicitly listed as OUT of scope for the capstone?
options: A Hydra config file
A pytest test suite
A live trading connection and a multi-strategy portfolio
A single momentum-style factor signal
questions.explain: The brief deliberately excludes live trading, a web UI, hyperparameter search, and a multi-strategy portfolio to keep the scope achievable and well-built.

questions.q: What makes a capstone run 'reproducible,' per this lesson?
options: It never uses any randomness at all
It is config-driven, any randomness uses a seeded generator, and parameters/results are logged
It is rewritten from scratch every time it runs
It only runs inside a Jupyter notebook
questions.explain: Reproducibility here means a config file (not hard-coded constants) drives the run, randomness is seeded, and each run's parameters and key results are logged.
